value.body: ITIs teach trade skills — electrician, fitter, welder, mechanic, COPA (computer operator) and dozens more — in courses of 1 or 2 years. They run under the Directorate General of Training (DGT), Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship. Passing the All India Trade Test leads to a National Trade Certificate (NTC).

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Admission is usually merit-based on Class 10 or Class 12 marks, through online counselling run by each state's directorate of employment and training; a few states also hold entrance tests. Minimum qualification depends on the trade (Class 8, 10 or 12), so Class 12 pass students qualify for most trades.

value.title: At a glance
items: Government ITIs charge low fees; private ITI fees vary widely.
Affiliation matters: NCVT certification is recognised nationally, so check an institute's status before enrolling.
Common next steps: an apprenticeship, a technician job, self-employment, or lateral entry into a polytechnic diploma in many states.
Seats in some trades go unfilled while others are in high demand.

value.title: Number of ITIs in India
value.note: Older series (government + private ITIs); gaps between years are uneven. Recent counts are around 14,600+ after disaffiliation of some ITIs.
